info.name: Welcome to Payscribe API
info.description:
[Payscribe](https://www.payscribe.co) builds, launch, and embeds innovative payment products across Africa, leveraging contemporary financial infrastructure. Our integration enables businesses to scale financial services, facilitate local and international payouts, collect customer payments, create virtual accounts, issue virtual cards, and empower them to expand their economic reach and grow their customer base. #### Getting Started To start using Payscribe API, you need to: 1. Sign up for a a test account on the [Sandbox](https://sandbox.payscribe.ng) and once done you can proceed to going live [Payscribe account](https://app.payscribe.ng/auth/signup) 2. Obtain your API key 3. Test all endpoints with sandbox keys 4. Satisfied with the integration? Proceed with your UAT and once done go live - Receive payments from customers - Issue USD Card - Purchase airtime (local and international) - Purchase internet data (local and international) - Create savings for your customers - Pay electricity bills (prepaid and postpaid) - Pay cable subscription (GOTV, DSTV, Startimes) - Pay internet data (Spectranet, Ntel, etc. - Fund betting wallet (bet9ja, 1xbet, sportybet) - Send bulk SMS - Pay educational voucher (JAMB, NECO, etc.) - Print recharge cards (MTN, GLO, AIRTEL, 9MOBILE): api/payscribe/recharge/ print - Convert excess airtime to cash - Fund transport wallet (Cowry Pay) - Receive payments - Make financial verifications **API Request and Response** - API requests should be made in JSON format - API responses will be in JSON format - Use your API key as Bearer in the header of each request **Security** - Our API uses SSL encryption to ensure secure transactions - Use HTTPS protocol to make requests **Rate limit** Payscribe allows up to 60 API requests/sec. When you go beyond that cap, you will get an HTTP error code of 429. `{"message": "API rate limit exceeded" }` **Support** We are dedicated to assisting you with any inquiries regarding code or other aspects. We have so many tutorials to get you started. Explore our documentation, kindly contact us on [X (Formerly Twitter)](https://x.com/trypayscribe) with a friendly 👋 , contact our support team. **Non-breaking changes** Payscribe regularly introduces backward-compatible changes to our API to provide additional product features and capabilities. Non-breaking changes may be introduced without prior warning to users of the Payscribe API. Examples of non-breaking changes would be: - New API endpoints - Additional new optional API request fields/parameters for existing endpoints - Additional new optional HTTP headers in API requests for existing endpoints - Additional new fields in API response for existing endpoints - Additional HTTP headers in API response for existing endpoints - Modification of text field values, for instance in error messages - Introduction of new transaction statuses within a status class - Introduction of new required fields linked to specific payers (list of required fields for a given payer is available by API, client implementation should rely on API response to define whether a field is mandatory) - Increasing length of existing text fields in API requests - Adding new fields in callback endpoints The client implementation should be designed with the above in mind, so that non-breaking changes do not adversely affect the implementation. ### Breaking changes A breaking change refers to a change that requires an application update to continue working with the API. Examples of breaking changes would be: - Removing or renaming an API endpoint - Changing the accepted values for an API request fields - Adding new mandatory field to an API request body, outside of information required for processing a transaction - Change in an API response structure (renaming of fields) Whenever possible, a new major version will be introduced if a breaking change is introduced. In the event that a breaking change is unavoidable and a new major version in not possible (e.g., change in regulation, compliance) Payscribe will contact clients in advance to ensure there is sufficient time to update the client’s application. **How to Get started** Create an account on [Payscribe](https://app.payscribe.ng) and complete your KYC, this literally should take less than 5 minutes. You will also have access the [sandbox](https://sandbox.payscribe.ng) web app, where you can have a full understanding of your integration and Payscribe ecosystem After then your profile setting page on payscribe.ng to get the token. If you will be needing technical support to integrate the API or more requests, kindly use the [Contact form ](https://www.payscribe.ng/contact) sending us a mail in respect to your request, and we would be glad to work with you At [Developers Hub](#) you will find useful resources such as tutorials and SDKs for your choice of language. | **Environment** | **Base URL** | | --- | --- | | Sandbox (test mode) | [https://sandbox.payscribe.ng/api/v1](https://) | | Production (live mode) | [https://api.payscribe.ng/api/v1](https://) | **Be conscious of the Token, replace it with the token you generated on your profile page**

Response code and message in response body

- 200 = Success - 201 = Transaction Pending - Reverify using Payscribe trans_id or the ref passed - 400 = Bad Request, Something missing in your body request - 401 = User not authenticated - 403 = Forbidden request, Contact Support - 404 = Page Not found - 405 = Duplicate Transaction - 406 = Missing Required Information, Please check that you have provided all mandatory information - 407 = Invalid product code/token - 408 = Result Not Found - 409 = Invalid Amount to process. Transaction Limit - 410 = Insufficient money in your wallet - 434 = General Operator Side Error, Transaction Failed - 435 = General Database Error, Transaction Failed - 5xx = Some server-side error Please if you have any challenge/suggestion with the API kindly send us a mail [hello@payscribe.ng](https://)

Events (Webhook)

Use webhooks to get notified about transaction events that happen in your Payscribe account. **What is a Webhook** A WebHook is an HTTP callback: an HTTP POST that occurs when something happens; a simple event-notification via HTTP POST. A web application implementing WebHooks will POST a message to a URL when certain things happen. In Payscribe you can setup webhooks that would let us notify you anytime events. Please note that you will find webhooks folder in each section of your integration.

item.name: Webhook Security & Signature Verification

request.description:
## Payscribe Webhook Security

Every webhook POST Payscribe sends to your endpoint includes **four security headers**.  
You should validate all of them before trusting the payload.

---

### Headers sent on every delivery

| Header | Example value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Payscribe-Event-Id` | `3f8a2e1b-…` | Unique event UUID - use for idempotency |
| `X-Payscribe-Timestamp` | `1712745600` | Unix timestamp of delivery |
| `X-Payscribe-Signature` | `v1=4a3f…` | HMAC-SHA256 signature (see below) |
| `X-Payscribe-Event` | `invoice.paid` | Event type - route without parsing body |
| `Idempotency-Key` | `3f8a2e1b-…` | Same as Event-Id, for safe retries |

---

### How the signature is built

```
base      = timestamp + "." + event_id + "." + rawBody
signature = HMAC-SHA256(base, your_secret_key)
header    = "v1=" + hex(signature)

 ```

- **`timestamp`** — the value from `X-Payscribe-Timestamp`
    
- **`event_id`** — the value from `X-Payscribe-Event-Id`
    
- **`rawBody`** — the **exact** raw bytes of the request body (do **not** parse then re-serialise)
    
- **`your_secret_key`** — your live or sandbox secret key from the Payscribe dashboard (`sk_live_…` / `sk_test_…`)
    

---

### Replay attack protection

Reject any webhook where:

```
abs(time() - X-Payscribe-Timestamp) > 300   // older than 5 minutes

 ```

---

### Idempotency

Store the `X-Payscribe-Event-Id` in your database and skip processing if you've seen it before.  
Payscribe retries failed deliveries with the **same** Event-Id, so this prevents double-processing.

## Verifying the signature — Python

``` python
import hashlib, hmac, time
from flask import Flask, request, abort
app = Flask(__name__)
PAYSCRIBE_SECRET = 'sk_live_your_secret_key'
def verify_payscribe_signature(secret: str) -> bool:
    event_id   = request.headers.get('X-Payscribe-Event-Id', '')
    timestamp  = request.headers.get('X-Payscribe-Timestamp', '')
    sig_header = request.headers.get('X-Payscribe-Signature', '')  # "v1=<hex>"
    raw_body   = request.get_data(as_text=True)  # raw bytes as string
    # 1. Validate header format
    if not sig_header.startswith('v1=') or len(sig_header) != 67:
        return False
    given_sig = sig_header[3:]
    # 2. Replay protection
    try:
        if abs(time.time() - int(timestamp)) > 300:
            return False
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return False
    # 3. Recompute HMAC
    base = f"{timestamp}.{event_id}.{raw_body}"
    calc = hmac.new(secret.encode(), base.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    # 4. Constant-time comparison
    return hmac.compare_digest(calc, given_sig)
@app.route('/webhooks/payscribe', methods=['POST'])
def webhook():
    if not verify_payscribe_signature(PAYSCRIBE_SECRET):
        abort(401, 'Signature verification failed')
    event = request.get_json(force=True)
    match event.get('event_type'):
        case 'bills.*':
            pass # handle
        case 'cards.*':
            pass # handle
        case 'invoice.paid':
            pass  # handle
        case 'payment_link.paid':
            pass  # handle
        case 'savings.contribution.success':
            pass  # handle
    return 'OK', 200

 ```

## Common mistakes to avoid

### 1\. Parsing the body before verifying

**Wrong** - `json.loads(request.body)` then re-serialising will produce different bytes if key order changes.

**Correct** - Read the **raw request body** first, verify the signature, then parse.

---

### 2\. Using `==` instead of a constant-time comparison

**Wrong** - `calc == given_sig` leaks timing information, enabling signature forgery.

**Correct** -`hash_equals($calc, $givenSig)` (PHP) / `crypto.timingSafeEqual(...)` (Node.js) / `hmac.compare_digest(...)` (Python).

---

### 3\. Skipping the timestamp check

**Wrong** - Not validating the timestamp allows an attacker to replay a captured webhook indefinitely.

**Correct** - Reject any request where `abs(now - timestamp) > 300`.

---

### 4\. Not implementing idempotency

**Wrong** - Processing the same event twice because Payscribe retried a delivery you didn't acknowledge in time.

**Correct** - Store `X-Payscribe-Event-Id` in a DB column with a UNIQUE constraint and skip duplicates.

---

### 5\. Returning a non-2xx status on success

Payscribe considers any response outside `2xx` a failure and will retry.  
Always return `HTTP 200` once you've accepted the event, even if your downstream processing is async.

### GET /data/lookup

This endpoint retrieves data plans for a specific network.

#### Request Parameters

- `network` (optional, String): This parameter specifies the network for which you want to lookup data plans. Accepted values are mtn, airtime, glo, or 9mobile, dstvshowmax
    
- category (optional: String): Some network providers have different categories of data plan, the most common one are gifting, awoof, corporate, and sme. You can filter by passing the category you want
    

To vend for ntel, spectranet, and other networks, please refer to the [/internet](https://documenter.getpostman.com/view/7369921/2s8YmRP1oT?version=latest#bee61911-74bc-4f45-bfa0-45bf250e3d24) page.

#### Response

The response will have a status code of 200 and a content type of application/json. The response body will contain the following fields:

- `status` (Boolean): Indicates the status of the response.
    
- `description` (String): Provides a description of the response.
    
- `message` (Object): Contains details about the data plans for the specified network, including network name, title, network code, check balance, logo URL, and plans.
    
    - `details` (Array): Contains information about the network, including its name, title, code, balance check, logo URL, and available plans.
        
        - `network_name` (String): Name of the network.
            
        - `title` (String): Title of the network.
            
        - `network_code` (String): Code of the network.
            
        - `check_balance` (String): URL for checking balance.
            
        - `logo_url` (String): URL of the network's logo.
            
        - `plans` (Array): Contains details of the available data plans.
            
            - `plan_code` (String): Code of the plan.
                
            - `name` (String): Name of the plan.
                
            - `alias` (String): Alias of the plan.
                
            - `amount` (String): Amount of the plan.
                

Example Response Body:

``` json
{
    "status": true,
    "description": "",
    "message": {

                "network_name": "",
                "title": "",
                "network_code": "",
                "check_balance": "",

                "plans": [
                    {
                        "plan_code": "",
                        "name": "",
                        "alias": "",
                        "amount": ""
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    },
    "status_code": 0
}

 ```

### HTTP POST /data/vend

Purchase data for Glo, MTN, Airtel, 9mobile, and DSTVShowmax.

It is advisable to call `GET /data/lookup` first to get the current `plan` code and amount before vending.

#### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| network | String | required | Network provider: `mtn`, `glo`, `airtel`, `9mobile`, `smile`, `dstvshowmax` |
| plan | String | required | Plan code from `/data/lookup` (e.g. `PSPLAN_177`) |
| recipient | String \| Array | required | Single phone number **or** array for bulk purchase (same network) |
| ref | String | optional | Your unique transaction reference |

#### Bulk Purchase

To vend the same plan to multiple numbers on the same network, pass `recipient` as an array:
```json
{
    "network": "mtn",
    "plan": "PSPLAN_177",
    "recipient": ["08169254598", "07012345678", "08012345678"],
    "ref": "my-batch-ref-001"
}
```

Each number in the array is validated and processed independently. Invalid numbers are skipped and returned in the `errors` field of the response.

#### Response

```json
{
    "status": true,
    "description": "Order received. Transaction in progress.",
    "message": {
        "details": {
            "processed": [{"number": "", "amount": 0, "id": "", "response": ""}],
            "transaction_status": "processing",
            "total_charge": 0,
            "trans_id": "",
            "created_at": ""
        }
    },
    "status_code": 200
}
```

### Get Wallet Ledger

#### Description

Returns a paginated, double-entry ledger of every movement on your Payscribe wallets. Each row represents a single credit or debit against a specific wallet account (`available`, `collection`, or `due`). This is the authoritative record for reconciliation.

#### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | string | No | Filter by currency code — `NGN`, `USD`, `USDT`, `USDC`, etc. Returns all currencies when omitted. |
| `direction` | string | No | `debit` or `credit` |
| `kind` | string | No | Movement category. Common values: `va_funding`, `payout`, `card_topup`, `card_withdraw`, `fee`, `refund`, `adjustment`, `crypto_settlement`, `collection_sweep`, `internal_fx` |
| `start_date` | string | No | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `end_date` | string | No | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `page` | integer | No | Defaults to `1` |
| `page_size` | integer | No | Defaults to `20`, max `100` |

| Field | Description |

| `id` | Ledger entry ID |
| `currency` | Wallet currency |
| `account` | Sub-account: `available`, `collection`, or `due` |
| `direction` | `credit` (money in) or `debit` (money out) |
| `amount` | Movement amount |
| `balance_before` | Wallet balance immediately before this movement |
| `balance_after` | Wallet balance immediately after |
| `kind` | Movement category |
| `description` | Human-readable note |
| `link_id` | UUID linking this entry to the originating transaction |
| `ref_id` | Your optional reference ID |
| `created_at` | Timestamp |

### HTTP POST /payouts/transfer — Bulk

Send money to **multiple bank accounts** in a single API call by passing a `rows[]` array. Each row is validated and queued independently. Your wallet is debited once for the total.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rows | Array | required | Array of transfer objects (no hard cap, but stay within your daily limit) |
| rows[].bank_code | String | required | Bank sort code (get from `GET /payouts/bank/list`) |
| rows[].account_number | String | required | 10-digit NUBAN account number |
| rows[].amount | Number | required | Amount in NGN (minimum NGN 100 per row) |
| rows[].narration | String | optional | Description shown on recipient statement |
| rows[].country | String | optional | Country code, defaults to `NG` |
| ref | String | optional | Batch reference; individual rows can include their own `ref` |

> **Security note:** Bulk transfers require your IP address to be whitelisted. Add it in **Settings → Security** on the Payscribe dashboard before calling this endpoint.

> Each row must pass account validation. Rows with invalid `account_number` or `bank_code` are rejected before any funds move — no partial debits on validation failures.

#### Response

Returns a batch summary with individual `processed[]` entries, a `batch_id` for tracking, and the combined `total_charge`:

```json
{
    "status": true,
    "description": "Batch transfer accepted.",
    "message": {
        "details": {
            "batch_id": "<uuid>",
            "processed": [
                {"account_number": "", "bank_code": "", "amount": 0, "id": "", "status": "processing"}
            ],
            "total_charge": 0,
            "transaction_status": "processing",
            "created_at": ""
        }
    },
    "status_code": 200
}
```

Use `GET /payouts/verify/:trans_id` to poll each individual transfer's final status.

item.description:
Virtual accounts is a unique account information consisting of account number and bank , which allows Payscribe busineses to receive payments from customers via bank transfer. Currently Payscribe ONLY support NGN virtual accounts.

> Please note: Virtual accounts does not store any monetary value like regular bank account number. It is only a means for your customers to pay you for a service and in return they must use the service(s) they pay you for on your platform. The payment gets settled in your account NGN Collection balance.  
Also, Payscribe does not store keep track of the money sent to the virtual account. The money is sent to your Payscribe collection balance once received. 
  

There are basically two types of virtual account numner.

**1\. Temporary Virtual Accounts:** This is also known as the dynamic account, and it is used to receive one-off payments. A typical use-case is when a customer is at the check-out point, you can generate this account with an expiry time for the customer to complete the transaction.

Please note that the virtual account becomes inactive (Not to be used once the time set as expired).

**2\. Permanet Virtual Accounts:** Also known as the static virtual account number. This does not have an expiry date/time and can be assigned to your customer for wallet funding on your app/website. Which also subsequent wallets funding for that customer.

**Requirements

**To create a permanent Virtual account, you need to create customer by calling the create customer endpoint, upgrade the customer to tier 1. You can also create customer on the fly, while creating the account.

**Supported Banks**

| **S/N** | **Bank Name** | **Value** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 9PSB Microfinance Bank | 9psb |
| 2 | Palmpay | palmpay |
| 3 | Cashconnect MFB | cashconnect |

## Create Quote - Currency Pair

This endpoint allows you to create a currency exchange quote between two currencies. It is typically used to determine the exchange rate and the amount the recipient will receive before initiating a currency conversion or transfer.

### PLEASE NOTE
Payscribe ONLY allows 20 calls / 24hours for normal businesses. Any additional call will incur USD0.3

### Purpose
Use this endpoint to obtain a real-time quote for converting a specified amount from one currency to another. The quote includes the exchange rate, calculated amounts, fees, and validity period.

### HTTP Request
`POST {{BASE_URL}}currency-pair`

### Authorization
This endpoint requires Bearer Token authentication. Include the following header in your request:

```
Authorization: Bearer {{API Token}}
```

### Request Body Parameters
Send a JSON object in the request body with the following fields:

| Field   | Type   | Required | Description                                  |
|---------|--------|----------|----------------------------------------------|
| from    | string | Yes      | The source currency code (e.g., "NGN").      |
| to      | string | Yes      | The target currency code (e.g., "USD").      |
| amount  | number | Yes      | The amount to convert from the source currency. |

**Example:**
```json
{
  "from": "NGN",
  "to": "USD",
  "amount": 5000
}
```

### Successful Response
A successful response returns HTTP 200 and a JSON object with the quote details.

**Response Structure:**
```json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "Quote created successfully.",
  "message": {
    "details": {
      "quote_id": 109,
      "from": "NGN",
      "to": "USD",
      "rate": 0.0006358815225547176,
      "rate_mid": 0.0006358815225547176,
      "amount_from": 5000,
      "amount_to": 3.169869392773588,
      "fee": {
        "abs": 0,
        "pct": 0.3,
        "total": 0.00953822
      },
      "spread_bps": 0,
      "side": null,
      "created_at": "2025-10-18 10:42:20",
      "expires_at": "2025-10-18 10:43:20",
      "sig": "..."
    }
  },
  "status_code": 200
}
```

#### Response Fields
- `status`: Indicates if the request was successful.
- `description`: Message describing the result.
- `message.details`: Contains the quote details:
  - `quote_id`: Unique identifier for the quote.
  - `from`: Source currency code.
  - `to`: Target currency code.
  - `rate`: Exchange rate applied.
  - `rate_mid`: Mid-market rate at the time of quote.
  - `amount_from`: Amount in source currency.
  - `amount_to`: Amount in target currency after conversion.
  - `fee`: Object with absolute (`abs`), percentage (`pct`), and total (`total`) fee values.
  - `spread_bps`: Spread in basis points.
  - `side`: Transaction side (if applicable).
  - `created_at`: Quote creation timestamp.
  - `expires_at`: Quote expiration timestamp.
  - `sig`: Signature for quote integrity verification.

### Notes
- The quote is valid only until the `expires_at` timestamp.
- Always check the `rate` and `fee` before proceeding with a transaction.

---

For more details, refer to the [Welcome to Payscribe API](collection/7369921-ee255f43-2394-447d-b30e-17ddd0e799fb).

## Execute A Quote

This request executes a currency conversion quote previously created via the Payscribe API. It finalizes the conversion transaction based on the provided quote details.

### Purpose
Use this endpoint to confirm and execute a currency conversion using a valid quote. Upon success, a conversion transaction is created and its details are returned.

### Authorization
- **Header:** `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`
  - Replace `<API_KEY>` with your valid Payscribe API key.

### Request Body
Send a raw JSON object with the following parameters:

- `quote_id` *(integer, required)*: The unique identifier of the quote to execute.
- `sig` *(string, required)*: A cryptographic signature validating the request. This is typically generated based on your integration with Payscribe's security requirements.

**Example:**
```json
{
  "quote_id": 110,
  "sig": "0f79353c2e27e659119de496e7f02134d44807d8..."
}
```

### Successful Response
A successful execution returns HTTP status `200` and a JSON body with the following structure:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "Conversion created successfully.",
  "message": {
    "details": {
      "trans_id": "30ef97d5-c9b3-4aff-918e-eba6ed1c6811",

      "sig": "0f79353c2e27e659119de496e7f02134d44807d8..."
    }
  },
  "status_code": 200
}
```

#### Response Fields
- `trans_id`: Unique transaction identifier for the conversion.
- `quote_id`: The quote ID that was executed.
- `from`: Source currency code.
- `to`: Target currency code.
- `rate`: Conversion rate applied.
- `amount_from`: Amount in the source currency.
- `amount_to`: Amount in the target currency.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of the conversion creation.
- `sig`: Signature for response validation.

### Notes

- Only valid, unexpired quotes can be executed.

request.description:
### Create a Card Funded by Stablecoin

#### Description

Issues a new virtual USD card for a customer, funded by a stablecoin deposit (USDT or USDC) rather than your Payscribe USD wallet balance.

When this endpoint is called:
1. Payscribe finds or provisions a dedicated on-chain deposit address for the customer.
2. The response returns the deposit address and the exact stablecoin amount the customer must send.
3. Once the on-chain deposit is confirmed by the payment processor, the card is created automatically and a `cards.created` webhook is fired.

The order expires after **24 hours** if no deposit is received.

#### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customer_id` | string | Yes | UUID of the customer to issue the card to |
| `currency` | string | Yes | Must be `USD` |
| `brand` | string | Yes | `VISA` or `MASTERCARD` |
| `amount` | number | Yes | Card load amount in USD (minimum `1`) |
| `type` | string | No | `virtual` (default) |
| `ref` | string | Yes | Your idempotency reference |
| `payment_method` | string | Yes | Must be `stablecoin` to trigger this flow |
| `stablecoin_currency` | string | No | `USDT` (default) or `USDC` |
| `stablecoin_network` | string | No | `Tron` (default), `Ethereum`, `BNB`, etc. |
| `stablecoin_chain` | string | No | `TRC20` (default), `ERC20`, `BEP20`, etc. |

> **Note:** A card creation fee of **$2 USD** (or **$1** on paid plans) is added to the `amount`. The `amount` field in the response reflects the total you must deposit, inclusive of the fee.

#### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "Deposit address ready. Your card will be created once the deposit is confirmed.",
  "message": {
    "status": "pending_payment",
    "payment_method": "stablecoin",
    "address": "TRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "memo_tag": null,
    "currency": "USDT",
    "network": "Tron",
    "chain": "TRC20",
    "amount": 7.00,
    "expires_at": "2025-04-11T10:00:00+00:00"
  },
  "status_code": 200
}
```

#### What happens next

1. Your customer sends the exact `amount` in `currency` to the `address` shown.
2. Payscribe detects the deposit on-chain.
3. The card is created and the customer's `cards.created` webhook is fired with the full card object.
4. If the deposit does not arrive within 24 hours the order expires — call this endpoint again to get a fresh address.

### Top Up a Card via Stablecoin

#### Description

Adds funds to an existing active virtual card using a stablecoin deposit (USDT or USDC) rather than your Payscribe USD wallet balance.

When called:
1. Payscribe finds or provisions a deposit address tied to the card's owner.
2. The response returns the address and exact amount to send.
3. Once the deposit is confirmed on-chain, the card balance is increased automatically and a `cards.topup` webhook fires.

The order expires after **24 hours**.

#### URL Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `card_id` | UUID of the card to top up |

#### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `amount` | number | Yes | Amount in USD to add to the card (minimum `1`) |
| `ref` | string | No | Your idempotency reference |
| `payment_method` | string | Yes | Must be `stablecoin` |
| `stablecoin_currency` | string | No | `USDT` (default) or `USDC` |
| `stablecoin_network` | string | No | `Tron` (default), `Ethereum`, `BNB`, etc. |
| `stablecoin_chain` | string | No | `TRC20` (default), `ERC20`, `BEP20`, etc. |

> **Note:** There is no additional fee for stablecoin top-ups. The `amount` in the response matches what you passed — it is the exact stablecoin value to deposit.

#### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "Deposit address ready. Your card will be topped up once the deposit is confirmed.",
  "message": {
    "status": "pending_payment",
    "payment_method": "stablecoin",
    "address": "TRxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "memo_tag": null,
    "currency": "USDT",
    "network": "Tron",
    "chain": "TRC20",
    "amount": 10.00,
    "expires_at": "2025-04-11T10:00:00+00:00"
  },
  "status_code": 200
}
```

#### Supported Networks

| Network | Chain | Currency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tron | TRC20 | USDT, USDC |
| Ethereum | ERC20 | USDT, USDC |
| BNB Smart Chain | BEP20 | USDT, USDC |

> Always send the **exact amount** shown. Sending more or less may delay settlement or require manual reconciliation.

item.description:
## Stablecoin Cards

Pay for card creation and top-ups using on-chain stablecoins (USDT or USDC) instead of your Payscribe USD wallet balance.

This flow is ideal when:
- Your customers hold crypto and want to fund their cards directly from a wallet.
- You want to avoid pre-funding your Payscribe USD balance before issuing cards.
- You need to support Web3-native payment flows in your product.

### How it works

1. Call the **Create Card** or **Top Up Card** endpoint with `payment_method: "stablecoin"` added to the request body.
2. Payscribe returns a deposit address and the exact stablecoin amount required.
3. The customer sends the stablecoin to the address on-chain.
4. Once confirmed, Payscribe creates the card or adds the funds automatically.
5. A webhook event fires to notify your system.

### Supported Stablecoins

| Stablecoin | Networks |
| --- | --- |
| USDT | Tron (TRC20), Ethereum (ERC20), BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) |
| USDC | Tron (TRC20), Ethereum (ERC20), BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) |

### Important Notes

- Card creation includes a fee (`$2` standard, `$1` on paid plans). The fee is included in the deposit amount returned.
- Top-ups carry **no additional fee** — deposit exactly the USD amount you want on the card.
- Orders expire after **24 hours**. Call the endpoint again to get a fresh address.
- The deposit address is **customer-scoped**: any future card operations for the same customer on the same network reuse the same address.

# Card Issuance ### Overview This folder contains the core APIs for issuing and managing cards to your customers -both individuals and businesses. All issued cards are virtual by design, but they can either be: - **Virtual Card**: A basic virtual card, not enabled for contactless payment methods. - **Contactless Virtual Card**: A full-featured virtual card that supports contactless payment channels like **Apple Pay**, **Google Pay**, and other tokenization services. These endpoints allow you to issue cards across various use cases while enabling control, flexibility, and digital accessibility. **Comparison Between Virtual Card Vs Contactless Virtual Card** | **Feature** | **Virtual Card** | **Contactless Virtual Card** | | --- | --- | --- | | Can be used online | Yes | Yes | | Supports contactless payments | No | Yes ( e.g Apple pay, google pay) | | Reloadable | Yes | Yes | | Can be added to digital wallets | No | Yes | | Custom MCC Whitelisting/Blacklisting | No | Yes | | Custom MID Blocking/Unblocking | Yes | Yes | | Suitable for: | Basic online transactions | Basic online transactions + Rich digital wallet experience | **Please note that we currently suppport USD Card.** **How Card Issuing Works** 1. Create customer if not already existing. 2. Enroll customer to Tier 2 Or use the Create Customer - Full endpoint to avoid upgrading customer. 3. Create a new card, select between virtual and contact virtual card 4. Configure controls such as daily or transaction limits 5. Whitelist or blacklist MCCs to manage card usage **Where Can the Card be used?** Payscribe Virtual card works on mostly US merchants, if you encounter any issue or need more clarity please contact [hello@payscribe.co](https://mailto:hello@payscribe.co) **Restricted MCCs** There are several merchant sites where the cards may be rejected. Tracks | #### **Summary** - All cards issued via these endpoints are **virtual** in form. - **Contactless Virtual Cards** support advanced digital wallet integrations (e.g., Apple Pay, Google Pay). - Contactless Cards are available on Mastercard and Visa cards. - NGN cards (currently not available) do not support contactless functionality. - Reloadability depends on user needs; use the **Lite Card** endpoint to issue cards that are for one-time use. - The choice between issuing a Virtual Card or a Contactless Virtual Card is determined by the payload parameters. request.description:
Payscribe sends a **POST** request to your configured webhook URL when this event fires.

**Event:** `savings.contribution.success`

**Security** — Every webhook request includes an `X-Payscribe-Signature` header. Verify it before processing:
```
HMAC-SHA256(secret_key, raw_request_body)
```

Fired after each successful scheduled contribution.

**Payload shape**
```json
{
  "event": "savings.contribution.success",
  "plan_id": 42,
  "customer_id": "cust-uuid",
  "trans_id": "sv_tx_uuid",
  "amount": 50000,
  "currency": "NGN",
  "balance_after": 150000,
  "created_at": "2026-05-01T09:00:30Z"
}
```

**Responding** — Return `HTTP 200` to acknowledge. Any non-2xx response will trigger retries (up to 5 attempts, exponential back-off).

item.description:
Create and manage automated savings plans for your customers.

**How it works**
1. Create a plan for a customer — specify the contribution amount, frequency, and start date
2. Payscribe schedules automatic contributions via cron (debiting from the customer's balance)
3. Funds accumulate in the plan's internal balance
4. The customer (or you via API) can withdraw to the business wallet at any time

**Plan types**
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `fixed` | Contributions run indefinitely on the set schedule |
| `target` | Contributions run until a `target_amount` or `target_date` is reached |

**Lock types**
| Lock | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `flexible` | Funds can be withdrawn any time |
| `locked` | Funds are locked until the maturity date; early withdrawal may incur a penalty |

**Missed contribution policies**
| Policy | Behaviour |
|--------|-----------|
| `retry_until_success` | Keeps retrying on the configured interval until success |
| `skip_and_continue` | Skips the missed cycle and continues as normal |
| `pause_on_failure` | Pauses the plan after the first failure |

request.description:
### Create Stable Address

This endpoint allows you to create a stable address for cryptocurrency transactions. It is specifically designed to handle requests for creating addresses in various cryptocurrency networks.

#### **Request Method**

- **POST**
    

#### **Request URL**

- `https://sandbox.payscribe.ng/api/v1/stable/address/create`
    

#### **Request Body**

The request should be sent in JSON format with the following parameters:

| **Parameter** | **Type** | **Mandatory** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| currency | String | Yes | The currency for which the address is being created (e.g., USDT). |
| network | String | Yes | The network on which the currency operates (e.g., Tron). |
| chain | String | Yes | The specific blockchain chain (e.g., TRC20). |
| label | String | Yes | A label for the address to help identify it (e.g., "Tomiwa USDT"). |
| customer_id | String | Yes | The unique identifier for the customer requesting the address. |

#### **Response Format**

Upon a successful request, the server will respond with a JSON object containing the following structure:

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "",
  "message": {
    "details": {
      "id": 0,
      "currency": "",
      "network": "",
      "chain": "",
      "address": "",
      "memo_tag": null,
      "is_primary": true,
      "created_at": "",
      "off_ramp_methods": [""],
      "limits": {
        "daily_quote": 0,
        "monthly_quote": 0
      }
    }
  },
  "status_code": 0
}

 ```

#### **Notes**

- A successful response will have a status code of **200**.
    
- The `message.details` object will contain information about the created address, including its unique ID, currency, network, and other relevant details.
    
- Ensure that all mandatory parameters are included in the request to avoid errors.
    

This endpoint is essential for users looking to generate stable addresses for their cryptocurrency transactions in a seamless manner.

### Retrieve Address Details

This endpoint retrieves the details of a specific address associated with a user. The request is made using the `GET` method and requires the unique identifier of the address in the URL.

#### **Request**

To fetch the details of an address, send a `GET` request to the endpoint:

```
GET {{BASE_URL}}stable/addresses/{address_id}

 ```

Where `{address_id}` is the unique identifier of the address you want to retrieve.

#### **Expected Response**

A successful response will return a JSON object with the following structure:

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "",
  "message": {
    "details": {
      "id": 0,
      "user_id": null,
      "customer_id": "",
      "currency": "",
      "network": "",
      "chain": "",
      "address": "",
      "memo_tag": null,
      "label": "",
      "tracking_id": "",
      "provider": "",
      "is_primary": true,
      "status": "",
      "created_at": ""
    }
  },
  "status_code": 0
}

 ```

#### **Response Fields**

- **status**: Indicates the success of the request (boolean).
    
- **description**: Additional information about the response (string).
    
- **message**: Contains the details of the address.
    
    - **details**:
        
        - **id**: Unique identifier for the address (integer).
            
        - **user_id**: Identifier for the user associated with the address (nullable).
            
        - **customer_id**: Identifier for the customer (string).
            
        - **currency**: Currency type associated with the address (string).
            
        - **network**: Network type (string).
            
        - **chain**: Blockchain chain information (string).
            
        - **address**: The actual address (string).
            
        - **memo_tag**: Optional memo tag (nullable).
            
        - **label**: Label for the address (string).
            
        - **tracking_id**: Tracking identifier (string).
            
        - **provider**: Provider information (string).
            
        - **is_primary**: Indicates if this is the primary address (boolean).
            
        - **status**: Current status of the address (string).
            
        - **created_at**: Timestamp of when the address was created (string).
            
- **status_code**: Code representing the status of the response (integer).
    

#### **Notes**

- Ensure that the `address_id` is valid to receive the correct address details.
    
- The response may vary based on the address status and associated user data.

request.description:
### Retrieve Address Details

This endpoint retrieves the details of a specific address associated with a user. The request is made using the `GET` method and requires the unique identifier of the address in the URL.

#### **Request**

To fetch the details of an address, send a `GET` request to the endpoint:

```
GET {{BASE_URL}}stable/addresses/{address_id}

 ```

Where `{address_id}` is the unique identifier of the address you want to retrieve.

#### **Expected Response**

A successful response will return a JSON object with the following structure:

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "description": "",
  "message": {
    "details": {
      "id": 0,
      "user_id": null,
      "customer_id": "",
      "currency": "",
      "network": "",
      "chain": "",
      "address": "",
      "memo_tag": null,
      "label": "",
      "tracking_id": "",
      "provider": "",
      "is_primary": true,
      "status": "",
      "created_at": ""
    }
  },
  "status_code": 0
}

 ```

#### **Response Fields**

- **status**: Indicates the success of the request (boolean).
    
- **description**: Additional information about the response (string).
    
- **message**: Contains the details of the address.
    
    - **details**:
        
        - **id**: Unique identifier for the address (integer).
            
        - **user_id**: Identifier for the user associated with the address (nullable).
            
        - **customer_id**: Identifier for the customer (string).
            
        - **currency**: Currency type associated with the address (string).
            
        - **network**: Network type (string).
            
        - **chain**: Blockchain chain information (string).
            
        - **address**: The actual address (string).
            
        - **memo_tag**: Optional memo tag (nullable).
            
        - **label**: Label for the address (string).
            
        - **tracking_id**: Tracking identifier (string).
            
        - **provider**: Provider information (string).
            
        - **is_primary**: Indicates if this is the primary address (boolean).
            
        - **status**: Current status of the address (string).
            
        - **created_at**: Timestamp of when the address was created (string).
            
- **status_code**: Code representing the status of the response (integer).
    

#### **Notes**

- Ensure that the `address_id` is valid to receive the correct address details.
    
- The response may vary based on the address status and associated user data.
